title: August 8: Let the Whole World Marvel at the Demonstration!
translatorNote: This translation is intended to carry Kalaignar's voice into clear, contemporary English rather than recast the letter as literary or academic prose. It preserves the source's argument, political directness, rhetorical questions, repetition, irony, factual detail, and paragraph order. Names, dates, figures, quotations, and intentional English expressions are retained. Where Tamil idiom cannot be reproduced literally without sounding unnatural, the English follows its sense and rhetorical force without adding claims absent from the source. The original Tamil is reproduced in full below the translation and remains the authoritative text. `Udanpirappē` is retained in Tamil transliteration rather than flattened into “brother,” “sister,” or “comrade.” Literally evoking “one born alongside me,” Kalaignar uses it as a distinctive address of shared identity, equality, affection, and solidarity within the movement.
paragraphs: At the meeting of the Tamil Eelam Supporters Organisation (TESO), held under my chairmanship at Anna Arivalayam in Chennai on 16 July 2013, four resolutions were adopted:

- insisting that Sri Lanka’s Thirteenth Constitutional Amendment be implemented in full; - urging India not to participate in the Commonwealth Conference to be held in Sri Lanka; - stressing the need to protect Tamil Nadu’s fishermen; and - demanding that Sinhala settlement in the Tamil regions of Sri Lanka be stopped.

To bring these four resolutions to the attention of the people of Tamil Nadu and the Union Government of India, and to unite the Tamil uprising against Sinhala domination, TESO decided to conduct a “Mass Tamil Demonstration” at about 10 a.m. on Thursday, 8 August, in every district headquarters across Tamil Nadu.

Accordingly, tomorrow’s protest will be held in Chennai under my leadership; in Madurai under the leadership of Tamil leader, my younger brother K. Veeramani; in Tiruchi under the leadership of DMK Treasurer, my younger brother M.K. Stalin; in Tiruvallur under the leadership of Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi leader Thol. Thirumavalavan; and in the other districts under the leadership of the front-ranking representatives of our movements. I have already written three letters so that this demonstration may be conducted successfully.
Even so, to explain to the public why this demonstration is being held, I wish to set out here a summary of the four resolutions adopted on the sixteenth.

On this issue, Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh has said that he is aware of attempts to weaken the Thirteenth Amendment and that efforts are being made to ensure that Tamil people and members of other communities in Sri Lanka are treated equally and with self-respect.

The Sri Lankan Government has so far honoured neither an agreement nor an assurance. The question, therefore, is how far it will honour the assurance now given by the Sri Lankan President to Shivshankar Menon.

Basil Rajapaksa, brother of the Sri Lankan President and a minister in the Sri Lankan Government, has stated that the present Government intends unilaterally to amend the agreement signed in 1987, without India’s consent. President Rajapaksa and his brother, Sri Lankan Defence Minister Gotabaya Rajapaksa, have also continued openly to state that they do not accept the Thirteenth Amendment.

No country has the authority unilaterally to violate or amend an agreement made between two nations. India’s own interests are also embodied in that agreement. Basil Rajapaksa’s declaration is therefore contrary to universally accepted practice.

TESO’s position is that the Thirteenth Amendment cannot constitute a complete political solution to the problem of the Eelam Tamils, and that a solution beneficial to them can be found only by holding a referendum among Eelam Tamils living in Sri Lanka and throughout the world and obtaining their opinion. Nevertheless, TESO considers that the Rajiv–Jayewardene Agreement should at least serve as an interim solution.
This meeting of TESO insists that the Government of India accept responsibility for ensuring that the 1987 Agreement is implemented exactly as written and without any amendment.

If the Commonwealth Conference is held in Sri Lanka, Rajapaksa will, by that very fact, become Chair of the Commonwealth for the following two years. Powerful arguments have therefore been advanced that it may become difficult to subject the head of an organisation of fifty-four countries to a judicial inquiry. If India calls Sri Lanka a friendly country and participates in the conference, it will amount to India accepting the genocide that occurred there. TESO has continually pressed the emphatic demand that India must not participate. This meeting urges the Government of India immediately to announce that India will not attend the Commonwealth Conference in Sri Lanka.

Whenever fishermen are arrested, political parties in Tamil Nadu issue appeals to the Union Government; TESO passes condemnatory resolutions and organises demonstrations; and the Tamil Nadu Government writes to the Prime Minister. None of this appears to have had any effect upon the Sri Lankan Government. This meeting therefore urges the Union Government at least now to take firm and immediate action that will resolve the problems of Tamil Nadu’s fishermen as a whole.

A resolution adopted by the United Nations Human Rights Council has stated categorically that, during an election period, districts must not be created, boundaries altered or new settlements encouraged. Yet the Sinhala Government is acting in violation of it. This meeting urges the Government of India to take note, bring the matter to the attention of the countries of the world and the United Nations Human Rights Council, and arrange for these actions to be stopped immediately.
Udanpirappē, it is to press these four resolutions that we are conducting tomorrow’s demonstration. This is not the first protest we have organised through TESO in support of the Eelam Tamils.

In the picketing campaigns conducted for the Eelam Tamils through TESO in 1985, 4,002 people participated in Chennai on 29 April; 3,000 in Tiruchi on the thirtieth; 1,000 in Dharmapuri on 3 May; 3,000 in Salem on the sixth; 6,000 in Thanjavur on the seventh; 2,500 in North Arcot on the eighth; 3,000 in South Arcot on the thirteenth; 1,500 in Periyar District on the fifteenth; 3,000 in Kanchipuram District on the sixteenth; 3,500 in Coimbatore and the Nilgiris on the seventeenth; 3,000 in Ramanathapuram, Pasumpon and Kamarajar districts on the eighteenth; 5,000 in Madurai District on the twentieth; and 5,500 in Tirunelveli, Kanyakumari and Puducherry on the twenty-second. All were arrested.
On 16 May 1985, I and a thousand others who went to participate in the picketing campaign at Kanchipuram to protect the welfare of the Sri Lankan Tamils were arrested and imprisoned.

TESO held massive processions on the Sri Lankan Tamil issue at Coimbatore on 3 October 1985, Dindigul on 4 October, Thoothukudi on 5 October, Tiruchi on 6 October, Salem on 7 October and Vellore on 13 October. A conference in support of the Eelam Tamils was held at Madurai on 4 May 1986.
Last year, on 12 August 2012, TESO held the “Eelam Tamils’ Right to Life Protection Conference” in Chennai.

Condemning the Sri Lankan Navy’s continuing harassment of Tamil Nadu fishermen, TESO resolved to conduct protest demonstrations at Rameswaram on 18 February 2013 and Nagapattinam on 19 February. Those peaceful demonstrations were held with the overwhelming support of the Tamil people.

On 5 March, TESO conducted a siege protest at the Sri Lankan Deputy High Commission in Chennai to condemn Sri Lankan President Rajapaksa as a war criminal who had violated human rights. On 7 March, leaders of all political parties and representatives of various humanitarian organisations participated in a special TESO conference and seminar in Delhi. To insist that the Indian Government support the resolution brought by the United States condemning the Sri Lankan Government’s genocide, a general strike was conducted throughout Tamil Nadu on 12 March 2013.

At the TESO meeting held on 15 April 2013, it was resolved that the cession of Katchatheevu to Sri Lanka through an agreement was constitutionally invalid; that the 1974 Agreement must therefore be annulled; and that the Supreme Court should be approached through TESO for a declaration that Katchatheevu is part of India. A case was accordingly filed in my name in the Supreme Court. The Court admitted it and directed the Union Government to file its counter-affidavit.
Tomorrow’s TESO demonstration throughout Tamil Nadu is a continuation of these struggles.

Meanwhile, the filing of nominations for the elections to the Northern, North Western and Central Provincial Councils in Sri Lanka, scheduled for 21 September, concluded on 2 August 2013. Speaking in that context, Sri Lankan Prime Minister D.M. Jayaratne stated that the Provincial Councils’ police powers and rights over land would be taken away. His statement reveals the scheme to dilute the Thirteenth Amendment and create in the Northern Province a “puppet” government possessing no real rights. Tomorrow’s demonstration is intended to oppose precisely this.

It is our duty to make this demonstration a success. I shall personally lead the demonstration in Chennai and meet there the valiant Udanpirappugal who will arrive with their voices raised. Tomorrow is the August 8 demonstration. Let the whole world marvel at the great multitude of Tamils!
With affection, M.K.
7 August 2013
